observation.visible_scene: A coastal sunset/sunrise scene: a vividly colored sky with streaked orange, pink and teal clouds and the sun glowing near the horizon; an ocean band with a line of breaking waves in the mid-distance; and a foreground of wet, mirror-like sand that reflects the sky's orange and cyan tones. The horizon and overall framing stay fixed across the excerpt.
visible_changes: Ocean waves continuously roll and crest along the mid-distance line; the shape and position of the white foam crest shift subtly frame to frame.

The swash/foam edge at the shoreline undulates and, on balance, retreats slightly toward the end of the clip, changing the boundary between the thin water sheet and the wet sand (most noticeable on the right side, where more reflective sand is exposed).
Reflections on the wet sand shimmer and their pattern shifts as the thin water layer moves; these are reflections of the sky, not separate objects.
The sky, cloud layout, and the sun's glow at the horizon remain essentially static over the ~2.7 s window (no clearly measurable cloud drift).
The horizon line and image composition do not move, indicating no detectable camera pan, tilt, or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the wave motion (wind, swell, tide) is not shown.
Whether the shoreline foam later advances again or fully drains away is beyond the excerpt.
The identity of a tiny dark speck near the right horizon in some early frames (possible distant person or bird) is not established.
uncertain_details: The exact phase of the swash cycle (advance vs. retreat) is subtle; the apparent net retreat is inferred from the slow change in the foam-edge position across many frames rather than a single frame.
Any cloud drift is too small to confirm against the static horizon.
The distant right-side speck appears and disappears between frames, so its motion is uncertain.
